newsitem.title: ISRAEL: IBM Israel takes 51 pct in Tadiran unit.
newsitem.headline: IBM Israel takes 51 pct in Tadiran unit.

text.p: IBM Israel has agreed to acquire a 51 percent stake in Israel's Tadiran Information Systems, a subsidiary of Tadiran Ltd, for $9.4 million in cash and assets, Tadiran said on Wednesday.
Together with the acquisition, the two sides will merge their computer service outsourcing businesses, which Tadiran estimated would achieve revenues of about $50 million this year.

"As a result of the transaction, Tadiran Information Systems will become the outsourcing arm of IBM Israel and a part of the worldwide service network of IBM Global Services," said Tadiran in a statement.
Outsourcing is the business of providing data processing services to companies on a contract basis. Tadiran said the combined companies had an orders backlog of about $73 million.

Under the accord, IBM Israel, a wholly own subsidiary of International Business Machines Corp, will pay $5.5 million in cash and transfer assets worth $3.9 million for the shares. It will also transfer contracts of an unspecificed value to Tadiran Systems.
Tadiran Systems, a software and information ssytems company, said it had sales last year of about $30 million.

Yisrael Zamir, managing director of Tadiran Ltd, which controls the remaining 49 percent of Tadiran Systems, said the accord was part of the company's strategy of finding multinational partners for its businesses.
In December, a Tadiran Electric Appliances Ltd official said an unnamed foreign company would be acquiring 26 percent of the company. Tadiran Appliances is 88 percent-controlled by Tadiran Ltd.
